Samir — quick technical notes from the SE side to help the upcoming session. TL;DR: both PrivateLink and VPC peering are viable; choice depends on control and routing simplicity.

PrivateLink (recommended when you want minimal route/ACL exposure):
- Works over AWS PrivateLink endpoints (AWS-managed ENIs). No cross-account route table changes required on your side.
- Pros: endpoint-based access, limited blast radius, IAM stays local.
- Cons: dependent on endpoint quotas and regional availability; additional per-endpoint cost.

VPC Peering (recommended if you need high-throughput lateral traffic):
- Simpler networking for large internal traffic volumes; routes must be configured across accounts.
- Pros: lower per-packet latency and cost in some topologies.
- Cons: route table maintenance and broader network exposure.

Egress IPs / allowlist options:
- We can provide a set of static egress IPs for Private VPC deployments by routing outbound through a NAT gateway managed in your account (recommended) or via a managed egress NAT in Redwood with assigned elastic IPs.
- If you need single static IPs per tenant, we typically recommend customer-managed NAT (your AWS account) where you control the EIPs. If you prefer Redwood-managed, we can allocate static EIPs but they are shared at a pool level and tied to the deployment.

On-prem connectivity options:
- Site-to-site VPN (IPsec) or Transit Gateway attachments are common. For legacy datacenters without BGP, we support an HTTP reverse-proxy to our ingress with mTLS; this is lower throughput but can be a pragmatic stop-gap.

KMS / HSM:
- We support customer-managed KMS for encrypting logs/artifacts at rest. HSM integration needs a short security review but is feasible for enterprise customers.

Prep for the deep-dive:
- Please provide expected requests/sec and average sequence length so we can size Dedicated vs Hosted routing patterns. If throughput is low (<25 qps) Hosted with PrivateLink is often simplest; for sustained high throughput we may recommend Dedicated capacity within your VPC.

Happy to cover these live in the session.
